faq.title: GAF Master Elite questions

items.question: What is the biggest benefit of hiring a Master Elite contractor?

children.text: Access to Golden Pledge on a qualifying roof, together with a contractor who meets GAF’s certification and renewal requirements. It gives you a broader choice of manufacturer protection when you replace your roof.

items.question: Is Golden Pledge automatically included with every Roof King roof?

children.text: No. The roof must qualify, and the enhanced warranty must be selected and registered. Ask which warranty is included in your proposal.

items.question: How is GAF-backed workmanship protection different from a product warranty?

children.text: Product coverage concerns manufacturing defects. Misapplication coverage concerns covered installation errors. Golden Pledge includes both, with the covered products, flashings, remedies and conditions defined in its written terms.

items.question: Does lifetime coverage mean the roof never needs replacing?

children.text: No. Lifetime is a defined warranty term tied to eligible ownership and property types; it is not a prediction of roof life or a promise against all damage.

faq.title: Siding questions: materials, installation and estimates

items.question: Is a full replacement needed for one damaged area?

children.text: Not automatically. The surrounding condition, cause and available matching material determine whether a local repair is practical. A wider replacement may be appropriate when deterioration or unresolved problems extend beyond the visible area.

items.question: Does new siding fix every wall leak?

children.text: No. The source needs to be identified and the relevant flashing, preparation or adjoining repair included. Cladding should not conceal an unresolved wall problem.

items.question: What should the estimate contain?

children.text: Look for the included elevations, selected material, removal, preparation, trim, flashing, fixture work, cleanup and additional-repair terms. Confirm applicable coverage for both the products and workmanship.

sections.title: Assessing siding damage before repair or replacement

cards.title: Repairing a limited area of damaged siding

children.text: A localized repair may be worth discussing where the surrounding wall and cladding remain serviceable. Suitability depends on the cause, compatible material availability and the ability to restore the connection. Matching can be limited by age, weathering or discontinued products. Confirm the repair estimate the team can provide for your siding.

cards.title: Checking flashing and moisture behind siding

children.text: Loose siding, damaged trim, staining and water near a window can arise from different failures. The assessment should consider the affected component and the neighboring details. A replacement panel alone may not resolve a failed flashing or moisture connection. Areas concealed by siding may require further investigation once material is removed.

cards.title: Checking the replacement profile and color

children.text: A repair panel needs a compatible profile, overlap and thickness as well as a similar color. We compare the panel shape and a physical sample against the existing wall in daylight. Weathering can change the appearance of older siding, so a matching color name alone does not guarantee an invisible repair.

The profile affects the roof's texture and shadow lines, while the color needs to work with the siding, masonry and trim that will remain. Use the GAF shingle styles and colors to narrow the options, then review the exact product and a sample. Availability and specifications can differ between lines; a brand name alone is not a product specification.

GAF shingle profiles, colors and specifications

GAF roof-system components beneath and around the shingles

The roof needs an appropriate supporting surface before new material is installed. The estimate should explain removal and the handling of damaged decking, along with the underlayment and any specified leak-barrier components.
Starter strips and ridge-cap shingles

Edges and ridge lines have their own component and fastening requirements. Identify the starter and ridge-cap products in the system proposal rather than assuming they are interchangeable with the field shingles.
Chimney, wall and vent flashing

Chimneys, walls, valleys and vents create transitions where water must be directed onto the roof surface. These details need a defined repair or replacement approach. New shingles do not correct an unrelated failed flashing connection by themselves.
Attic intake and exhaust ventilation

Attic and roof ventilation should be evaluated with the installation. The relevant product requirements and actual roof conditions determine the work; ventilation is not simply an accessory to add without considering the existing arrangement.
Planning GAF tear-off, preparation and installation

A roof replacement estimate should identify tear-off, preparation, products, connection details, cleanup and how concealed repairs will be handled. expectedBlocks: Water overflowing at a commercial roof edge can affect entrances, walls, loading areas and the ground around the building. Roof King helps Columbus property owners assess external gutters and downspouts as a connected drainage route. The useful starting point is where the water goes now and where the proposed system needs to take it.
Commercial gutter overflow: tracing the drainage problem
Gutter runs, outlets and the route beyond the building

Overflow can result from debris, damaged gutter sections, failed connections, limited outlet capacity or a discharge restriction. Deteriorated supports or fascia can also change how the gutter performs. Record the affected roof area and the weather conditions when the problem occurs. Staining on a wall identifies a symptom, but the assessment needs to establish the failing part of the route.
Commercial gutter layout: collection, discharge and attachment
Roof edge and collection areas

The size and arrangement of the contributing roof surfaces matter to the drainage design. One gutter may receive runoff from more than the area directly above it. Identify valleys, transitions and any areas that concentrate flow.
Outlets and downspouts

Outlets need to connect the gutter with an appropriate downspout arrangement. Their positions should account for entrances, walkways, loading operations and the building exterior. A wider gutter alone does not resolve an unsuitable outlet or discharge route.
Attachments and supporting construction

The system needs sound support and a compatible connection to the roof edge. Identify fascia, edge metal or other adjoining repairs before installing new gutters. The proposal should state which supporting components are retained or replaced.
External gutters, scuppers and internal drains have different roles

Some buildings also use internal drains, scuppers or below-ground drainage connections. These are different components with their own responsibilities and design requirements. Define the work included in the gutter proposal and identify any separate roofing, plumbing or site-drainage assessment needed.
Commercial gutter profiles, materials and connection details

Compare the proposed profile, size, finish, attachment and joint details as a complete system. Seamless gutters can reduce joints along straight runs, but corners and outlets still need connections. Confirm the product and fabrication approach suitable for the building rather than assuming a residential configuration can simply be extended.

Share the building address, areas of overflow and available roof information. Roof King can discuss the gutter work alongside any related commercial roofing needs.
Does replacing a gutter resolve water beside the building?
Only if the identified cause is addressed. Downspouts, underground connections or ground drainage may need separate attention. The estimate should describe the problem it is intended to resolve.

Discuss the building's requirements before scheduling. The possible sequence depends on access and the extent of the work; uninterrupted operations cannot be assumed.

Identifying the particular assembly matters when assessing surface damage, flashings or later repairs. The category name alone does not establish which repair or replacement method is appropriate.

These descriptions explain common systems; they are not a blanket offer to install every membrane or method. Roof King's proposed work should confirm the system it will service and the products it will use.
Shingle and metal roofs on commercial or multifamily buildings

Asphalt shingles and metal roofing can be relevant on sloped commercial or multifamily buildings. The roof geometry, supporting construction, occupancy and project access still need commercial planning. Compare commercial repair or commercial replacement with the building's actual conditions rather than selecting by property label alone.
Commercial roof assemblies: covering, insulation and connections

The deck supports the assembly. Insulation, cover boards and other layers may serve different functions depending on the design. Attachment transfers forces through the assembly, while perimeter and penetration details complete the connections. A proposal should identify the relevant layers and explain which existing components will remain.
Deck, insulation and the condition of retained layers

The membrane is the visible weather surface, but the deck and insulation below it influence the replacement decision. A wet or deteriorated layer needs assessment before another system is placed over it. Identify the layers being retained and the condition evidence supporting that choice.

TPO, PVC and EPDM are different material families. Their joining and repair products need to match the identified system. Color or a general description such as rubber roofing is not enough to specify a repair; existing records and the roof assessment help establish the actual covering.
Parapets, equipment curbs and drainage outlets

A commercial roof assembly ends and changes direction at edges, walls, curbs and outlets. Those connections need to be specified with the field covering. A material comparison should include the detailing needed to move water to the discharge points and preserve access for equipment service.

Low-slope does not mean that water movement can be ignored. The assessment needs to address the intended path to drains, scuppers or external gutters and the condition of those details. A new membrane is not automatically a correction for an unresolved drainage layout.

Sometimes a photograph narrows the possibilities, but it may not establish the exact product or assembly. Existing records and an assessment provide a better basis for repairs.

Suitability depends on the building, existing construction, drainage, intended use, installation requirements and budget. The useful comparison is between specified assemblies for the same property.

Roof King helps Columbus homeowners assess suspected damage, understand the condition of the roof and compare a defined repair with broader replacement where appropriate. A dent or photograph is a starting observation, not a complete roof diagnosis.
Suspected hail damage: what roof and metal observations can show
Surface changes, material condition and inspection limits

Changes on a shingle surface, damaged components or dents in exposed metal may justify closer inspection after hail. Similar-looking marks can also have other causes, including age, wear or earlier work. The material, pattern and surrounding condition need to be assessed together. Avoid climbing onto the roof to investigate.
Hail inspection observations: shingles, metal and adjoining exteriors
Covering and roof areas

Identify the affected slopes and material, with photographs tied to locations. A ground-level view may miss details, while a close view of one spot does not establish the condition of the entire roof. Areas that cannot be inspected should be noted.
Flashing, vents and exposed metal

These components can provide useful observations, but their condition should be recorded separately from the shingles. Damage to one material does not automatically establish equivalent damage to another.
Gutters and adjoining exterior components

Record affected gutters, siding or trim where relevant. Different components may require different repair estimates and material choices. A roof-only estimate should not imply that every exterior item is included.
Hail-damaged roofing: localized repair or wider replacement

A localized roof repair may be practical when the damage is limited, the surrounding materials remain serviceable and compatible components can be integrated. The working area may extend beyond the visible marks to restore the layers and connections appropriately.

Consider roof replacement when the findings show wider damage or a condition that cannot support a satisfactory repair. The recommendation should explain the extent and implications of the findings rather than assume every hail event requires a new roof. Matching and discontinued materials should also be discussed before choosing selective work.
Your hail repair estimate: materials, preparation and adjoining work

The permanent repair plan should identify material removal, preparation, replacement components and the connection to the retained roof. Any temporary protection is a separate measure with its own limitations and follow-up needs. Include cleanup, concealed-damage decisions and any separately required interior or exterior work.
Shingle impact classifications and the limits of hail protection

A published impact classification describes testing for a particular product under stated conditions. It does not make a roof hail-proof or establish that every real storm will have the same effect. Use the shingle product information to compare the actual product and applicable coverage if replacement material is being selected.
Tell Roof King when you noticed the concern, the property address and any visible changes or leaks. The next step is a record of the findings and a repair recommendation based on the actual roof.
Does a dented gutter mean the shingles need replacement?
Not by itself. The gutter and roofing need their own assessment. Observations from one component can help direct an inspection but do not determine the roof's repairability.
Can the inspection guarantee an insurance payment?
No. The construction findings and estimate describe the roof and proposed work. Coverage is determined through the policy and insurer. Keep the records explained on the storm documentation page.
What if the roof is leaking now?
Call and describe the active water entry so availability and the next step can be discussed. The local storm service explains the distinction between temporary response and permanent repairs.
